briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Awards, Acquisitions & a Pause on Rescheduling: The Industry Keeps Moving Forward
briefs.top: Michigan operators are racking up craft-cannabis accolades and political promises of tax relief even as regulators swing a hard enforcement hammer on bad actors. Nationally, Compass Pathways edges toward a historic psilocybin approval and MSOs keep consolidating, while a DEA judge's procedural pause on rescheduling is a speed bump, not a dead end.

local.text: Ann Arbor, Lansing brands sweep Best of Detroit weed awards — Information Entropy's converted-church dispensary and Hey! Captain's freeze-dried, nug-shaped edibles took top 2026 honors for craftsmanship and creativity.
Governor's race brings real shot at tax repeal — cannabis execs wrote ~$90K in checks backing GOP candidate John James, who's pledged to kill the 24% wholesale tax if elected.
Sen. Irwin urges industry caution on James's tax pledge — the Ann Arbor Democrat told Marijuana Moment that James hasn't backed cannabis reform in Congress despite now courting industry votes.
Menominee voters may open 4 new dispensary slots — a ballot measure this week asks to raise the city's store cap from 9 to 13, a fresh licensing opportunity up north.
CRA drops record-tying $2M fine, pulls 20 licenses — regulators nailed a Clare grower for shipping dirt and mulch instead of flower, a cleanup move that protects compliant operators' market standing.

national.text: Compass Pathways nears psilocybin NDA finish line — the company is targeting Q4 2026 to complete its rolling submission for COMP360 in treatment-resistant depression, with a possible H1 2027 launch.
White House order pours $50M into psychedelic research — the 2026 executive order pushes FDA to fast-track psychedelic reviews and directs DEA to cut research barriers, with ibogaine a top priority.
Verano readies Virginia for adult-use launch — the Chicago MSO is remodeling stores ahead of a July rollout, building on its $90M buy of Cannabist's Virginia operations.
DEA rescheduling hits a procedural pause, not a reversal — the chief judge stayed proceedings Sept. 29 over a new GAO report, with a government response due Oct. 13 before the case resumes.
Bipartisan lawmakers press White House for Schedule III clarity — four House members sent a letter to Trump and cabinet officials seeking guidance on the federal medical-cannabis framework.
